comment: Pinned upstream Docker CLI tooling (#66). Like the engine manifest, these
versions + per-arch URL + sha256 are compiled into the binary: nothing is
fetched as 'latest'. Bytes come from each upstream project's own release
assets. An arch entry with an empty sha256 is a placeholder — Published()
treats it as 'not available for this platform' and the installer skips it
with an honest message rather than importing anything unverified.
compose/buildx/wincred sha256 come from each project's published checksums
file (compose: checksums.txt; buildx: checksums-signed.txt, which is the one
that covers windows; wincred: checksums.txt).
The docker CLI is the exception, twice over (#450).
amd64: download.docker.com publishes no checksum, so its sha256 is computed
from the official download and pinned here. Every install still verifies the
exact bytes; the digest is just ours rather than upstream's.
arm64: upstream publishes no Windows arm64 docker.exe at all -- the static
tree has one directory, x86_64/, and docker/cli attaches no release assets.
So Skrog BUILDS this one, from docker/cli source at a commit-pinned tag,
and its URL points at a dockercli- release of this repository rather than
at Docker. See third_party/docker-cli/ and docs/docker-cli.md.
amd64 deliberately stays Docker's own bytes: anyone can re-download the zip
and check the digest below without reference to Skrog, and building it too
would put every user behind our build rather than only the arm64 users who
have no alternative. A test fails if the amd64 URL stops pointing at
download.docker.com, so changing that is a decision rather than a slip.
When upstream ships an arm64 build, both point at Docker again and
third_party/docker-cli/ is deleted.
Licenses: docker/cli, docker/compose, docker/buildx are Apache-2.0;
docker-credential-helpers is MIT. Stage() lays each LICENSE beside the
binaries (embedded from internal/dockercli/licenses).
